Things that bothered me immensely when I was a younger man, I don't even think about any more, and things I never cared about then keeps me awake at night now.

Societies also change. I can only only speak from my own experiences, but as a Samoan, I encountered racism a lot more as a kid than my half Samoan/half black children do. And when I was in high-school, no one, and I mean not a single soul, was openly gay. Were someone to come out of the closet, they probably would have been beaten and harassed not stop. Now, some of the "cool kids" at my kid's school are openly gay. We're becoming more tolerant, and we understand that not everyone has to be like us. We've got some a long way to still, but it seems that society itself gains wisdom with age, just as individuals do.

Change comes from within. It comes from seeing the error of not only your actions, but your ways of thinking. It comes from wanting to better oneself at any cost.

I used to have one hell of a temper. I never hit anyone, but I certainly could yell and scream, and I'd put the fear of God into people when I did. After my first divorce, I realized that while I didn't make her cheat on me, I certainly contributed. At the end of the day she still chose to be unfaithful, but my actions probably steered her in that direction. If she could see me now, she wouldn't see the same person. My current wife and I are extremely happy together. We're able to calmly talk things through and, after five years of being together, haven't had a single argument. We've had a couple of heated discussions, sure, but at the end of the day we always come to consensus. It's wonderful.
You can change a lot of things, your name, your appearance, your address, but you can't change your passions
Change is what people do. Slow, methodical, unnoticable change that creeps up on you. Think of you at age 12 vs. now.

All these answers are "Yes but very hard".

I tell you if you want to. You can. Simple.

Just for sake of example, I knew a smoker... And I mean a pack-a-day type of smoker. He told his wife that he would quit once their child is born. And he did! Just like that, overnight.
My grandfather was a long-term cigar smoker. My grandmother got sick and the doctors told the pair that it was likely because of my grandfather smoking around her. He quit that day.
People change all the time. They just don't like to be criticized.

Change is inevitable. Sometimes it moves at a snail's pace, and other times it's rapacious as fire, but it does happen. Pain forces change, whether it is from personal experience or outside stimulus. We don't enjoy pain. We change so that we don't feel that pain again, or even potential pain from fear.
I doubt it's possible for most people to change who they fundamentally are, however I think people can choose to change their actions. That's a huge thing, and in the end it's what's important.
